raw_response:
I’m 65 this year, and I’ve worked these fields all my life, so I don’t like making big changes unless there’s a clear reason. I’ve got only 11.6 mu, so every mu has to be arranged carefully. Cotton is still my main crop because I know it well and I have a well, but I won’t put all the land into one crop. Maize and wheat are the steady ones for grain, millet and mungbean don’t need as much input, and mungbean helps the soil a bit too. The extension people talk about precise rates, but in the end I still look at my own land and what farmers around me are doing. If cotton prices look decent, I’ll keep cotton on the better plots and use the rest for grain and small杂粮 so I’m not risking everything on one crop. Fertilizer I’ll use, but not too aggressively because input prices are real money. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I’ll save irrigation for the important stages.
